faqs.a: ICE stands for In Case of Emergency. Paramedics and hospital staff are trained to look for ICE contacts on phones and cards. A printed card works when your phone is locked, dead, or missing.
faqs.q: What does ICE mean on an emergency card?

faqs.a: Review it every 6 months or whenever something changes: new phone number, new medication, new allergy, or a new doctor. An outdated card can mislead responders, which is worse than no card.
faqs.q: How often should I update the card?

faqs.a: Include serious allergies (especially drugs, food, insect stings), chronic conditions (asthma, diabetes, epilepsy, heart disease), and current medications with doses if space allows. Skip minor issues; the card must stay scannable in seconds.
Blood group helps responders prepare, but hospitals always re-test before transfusion. Never rely on the card alone for transfusion decisions. The card speeds things up; the lab test decides.

emergency-contact-card-maker.formula:
Emergency card = identity (name) + medical facts (blood group, allergies, conditions, medications) + 2 contacts (name, relation, phone) + doctor + notes.
Keep it to one card: responders read it in under 30 seconds.
howTo: Fill your name, blood group, allergies, conditions, and medications.
Add two emergency contacts with their relation and phone numbers.
Optionally add your doctor and any extra notes.
Check the live card preview for typos, especially phone numbers.
Click Print card and cut it to wallet size. Keep it in your wallet.

mistakes: Never updating it — an outdated card with an old number is worse than no card. Review it every six months.
A typo in a phone number — the entire point of the card is that someone can call for you. Check every digit twice.
Leaving out serious allergies or medications — that's the information paramedics need most, and it's the part people forget.
Treating the blood group as gospel — hospitals re-test before transfusion anyway. Never delay urgent care waiting to 'confirm' the card.
Keeping it only in a locked phone — paramedics can't open a locked screen. A printed card in the wallet works when the phone doesn't.
